reason: The solver-check procedure let hidden reference solutions leak into an input meant to exclude them, a leak-of-hidden-data defect caught before use.
A range seen on winner checkpoints was over-generalized to all checkpoints, overstating the lower bound in the report.
A reported count of trained plans was inflated by including held-out plans, a miscount in a reported figure.
A wrong number copied from a neighbouring row was written into a report table.
Files were removed from the working directory by the environment with no project-code cause and restored from git.
The pruning procedure deleted run manifests that its own stated intent says must be kept, because they shared a directory with checkpoints.
A score gain was causally credited to new commands that item-level evidence shows few gained programs used.
A 20-of-20 result was attributed to container commands the saved programs do not use and over-generalized to solving the book.
An accuracy difference between models of different families was attributed solely to parameter count, an unsupported causal claim.
Scores on regenerated holdouts with changed items and references were compared as if they were the same test.
A regression diagnosis asserted item-level causes before reading the items, which differed only in punctuation.
The zero result on the common-sense book was given a causal explanation contradicted by the training records.
Percentages from an unrecorded subagent judging procedure were presented as measured semantic accuracy.
Exact string mismatch with prose references was taken as incorrectness although answers had the right value and verdict.
The experiment name 'qwen3-17b' was read as the identity of a 17B model although the run used Qwen3-1.7B.
The base choice compared scores on different item sets and counted missing responses as failures, treating unequal populations as comparable.
The memory guard took the driver's free-memory figure as the system's memory state although reclaimable cache made it unrepresentative.
The 'series done' log line, also written on failure, was taken as evidence that the chain completed successfully.
The disk filled overnight and corrupted a checkpoint mid-save, a resource failure the guard's thresholds failed to prevent.
Scripts stored in the temporary directory were removed by a machine reset.
An argument-parser bug made every launch exit immediately, and fixing it would have prevented the false completions downstream.
Base models' scores under a compiled-program format they were never trained on were taken as their baseline capability.
The retry loop recorded later attempts without executing them, so the code did not do what it was meant to.
The split function ignored declared evaluation reservations, contrary to its specified behaviour.
Appending correct values or plans in unseen wording changed the prompt distribution rather than isolating the supplied input.
A selection score dominated by seen plans and a repeatedly consulted holdout were taken as held-out generalization evidence.
The option leaked the target's reference solution into demonstration selection, data the runner was meant to exclude.
The scorer read the first number in the answer and ignored the probe's exact-comparison policy.
Falling strict-format probe scores were taken as loss of general capability although correct values were scored as mismatches.
Evaluation and resume read current working-tree inputs instead of the experiment's recorded training inputs, contrary to evident intent.
Incomplete running-chain checks, a missing lock, and stale lock handling produced a race between concurrent processes.
A shared alias and port were taken as the identity of the serving model, so records named a checkpoint that was not answering.
